title: Volume-confirmed 20-hour high break that must hold for two bars, intraday session-bounded
ex_ante_rule: Chart 1h, closed candles only; a signal at the close of bar t is filled at the open of bar t+1. Long only, spot, one position at a time, whole allowed balance, no pyramiding. Definitions at bar t: P(t) = highest high of the previous 20 bars (t-20..t-1, current bar excluded). VolAvg4(t) = arithmetic mean of volume of the previous 4 bars (t-4..t-1, current bar excluded). SMA40(t) = simple mean of close over the 40 bars ending at t (current bar included). ENTRY at the close of bar t when ALL hold: (1) close(t) > 1.002 * P(t); (2) volume(t) >= 2.0 * VolAvg4(t); (3) close(t) > SMA40(t); (4) the open time of bar t is between 00:00 and 16:00 UTC inclusive (bar open hour 0..16); (5) no position is open; (6) cooldown: no entry signal on the bar that closes the exit bar, i.e. no re-entry for 1 candle after any exit. On entry store P_entry = P(t) of the signal bar, fixed for the trade. FAIL-FAST EXIT: for the 2 bars after the signal bar (t+1 and t+2), if close(k) < P_entry, exit at the open of bar k+1. TRAILING EXIT: from bar t+3 onward, exit at the open of bar k+1 when close(k) < lowest low of the previous 4 bars (k-4..k-1, current bar excluded). Before bar t+3 only the fail-fast exit, the stop and the time exits apply. STOP-LOSS: fixed 2% below the fill price (native intrabar stop, triggers on touch). TIME EXITS (whichever comes first): (a) session flat: a position still open at the close of the bar that opens at 22:00 UTC is sold at the 23:00 UTC open; (b) maximum holding: sold at the open 12 hours after the fill (exit signal at the close of the bar that opens 11 hours after the fill). No take-profit, no other filters. Warm-up: 100 bars (longest lookback SMA40; no recursive indicators; margin for stability).
rationale: Livermore's pivotal-point idea: no position until price actually penetrates a significant prior high, the penetration must come with expanding activity, and a break that stalls or falls back is a danger signal to exit at once. Counterparties are stop orders of shorts and breakout buyers resting above the 20-hour high plus late followers; when real demand (a volume burst of at least 2x the last four hours) is behind the break, the order-flow imbalance tends to persist for some hours, while a break that closes back under the pivot within two bars shows the demand was absent, so the loss is cut small. The 40-hour mean keeps entries in the local up-leg; in a range or a falling market fewer closes sit above SMA40 with a volume burst, and the 2-bar fail-fast plus 2% stop limit each failed break. This is the parent H-046 (240/48/480-bar windows, 3/3 pairs at exploration, gross move 1.07% per trade) scaled to intraday by dividing the windows by twelve so trades close within the day. The volume burst is the activity filter the mechanism already implies (lesson a); the 00:00-16:00 UTC entry window and the 23:00/12h time exits are part of the idea, not added filters. Expected trades: roughly 150-400 per year per pair (20-bar highs with a volume burst are frequent on 1h). Expected gross move about 0.9% on winners and roughly 0.5% averaged (design estimate, not measured), above the 0.30% base round trip; winners are not capped, as lesson (b) advises.
novelty_vs_tried: Second variant of LivermorePivotFailFast (H-046 is the only one). H-046 is a multi-day swing rule: 240-bar pivot, 48-bar volume mean, SMA480, 8-bar fail-fast, 48-bar low trail, 4% stop, no time exit, so it does not meet the owner's day-trade requirement. H-108 keeps the same mechanism but on an intraday horizon: windows divided by twelve (20/4/40), 2-bar fail-fast, 4-bar low trail, 2% stop, entries only for bars opening 00:00-16:00 UTC and a mandatory flat at the 23:00 UTC open or after 12 hours. It differs from SessionOpeningRangeBreakout (session-open range) and HourlyFailedBreakdownReclaim (a long after a failed breakdown) in using a rolling prior-high pivot with volume confirmation and a failed-break exit.
